title: The for loop: invariants, boundaries, and cost
goal: Repeat a known number of steps and explain the state before and after every iteration.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.if-else-switch. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: The three header parts
paragraphs: for(init; condition; update) runs init once and tests condition before every iteration. update follows the body. If the first condition is false, the body never runs, making n=0 a natural case.
In for(int i=0; i<n; ++i), i exists in the condition, body, and update but not after the loop. It denotes the next index to process. The iteration count is n for a bounded nonnegative n.

sections.title: A half-open interval rather than a guess
paragraphs: The index range [0,n) includes 0 and excludes n, giving exactly n positions. Values 1 through n can use i=1; i<=n, but mixing the first version’s start with the second version’s condition changes the count.
For n=3, the body sees i=0,1,2; the i=3 check terminates the loop. That final value is tested but not processed. Confusing a check with an execution often causes an off-by-one error.

sections.title: Summing a half-open range
paragraphs: Before a step, sum contains the sum of [0,i).

sections.title: An invariant as a short proof
paragraphs: For the sum of n integers starting at zero, the invariant is: before each iteration, sum contains the sum of [0,i). At i=0 the range is empty, so sum=0. After sum+=i and ++i, the claim holds for the larger boundary.

When i==n, the invariant yields the required result. Prove termination separately: n-i is nonnegative before the body and decreases by one. A correct invariant cannot guarantee termination if the counter never advances.

sections.title: Accumulators and ranges
paragraphs: Initialize an accumulator before the loop and update it inside. Resetting it on every iteration retains only the final contribution. With n<=1000 and values between -1000 and 1000, the absolute sum is at most 1000000.

Use long long for broader bounds and justify intermediate values before addition. A larger type does not make unbounded input safe. Handle an extraction failure inside the loop instead of repeatedly adding an old value.

sections.title: Skipping odd values
paragraphs: continue does not skip the for update.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.

sections.title: break and continue
paragraphs: break exits the nearest loop. continue skips the rest of the body but still performs a for loop’s update. In filtering it can separate an unsuitable element, but it must not bypass the operation that obtains the next item.
Nested loops have separate counters; break exits only the inner loop. A complete r by c traversal performs r*c iterations. Establish dimension bounds before multiplying and estimating cost.

sections.title: Measuring work
paragraphs: A linear traversal performs work proportional to n: O(n), with O(1) extra memory for a fixed number of accumulators. This describes growth, not milliseconds or an exact instruction count.

Test n=0, n=1, the maximum n, and a failure midway through input. For a small n, record i, the condition, and sum before and after the body. Next, while will handle a stream whose length is not given in advance.

selfcheck.prompt: How many times does for(i=0;i<3;++i) execute?
selfcheck.feedback: The body sees i=0,1,2; i=3 is only tested.
An empty sum requires no element access.

selfcheck.prompt: Where is a total sum initialized?
selfcheck.feedback: Resetting in the body loses previous terms.

selfcheck.prompt: Does for execute its update after continue?
selfcheck.feedback: continue skips the body remainder and then update executes.

practice.title: Laboratory: The for loop: invariants, boundaries, and cost
practice.task: Read n from 0 to 100 followed by exactly n integers from -1000 to 1000; print their sum and positive count. Reject extra tokens and incomplete data as invalid.
criteria: The contract matches the task and defines units, empty input, and extra data.
Every published case matches and two explained original tests are included.
Before each iteration state which portion is already processed.
Do not reset the sum in the body. Test < versus <= only with a safe scalar counter.
Source, actual output, exit code, and a justified complexity explanation are preserved.
